source.title: Benign, Tempered, or Catastrophic: A Taxonomy of Overfitting
source.authors: Neil Rohit Mallinar; James B. Simon; Amirhesam Abedsoltan; Parthe Pandit; Mikhail Belkin; Preetum Nakkiran

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices and experimental details.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own noisy-label experiments on interpolating networks and argues that they fit the training data while test error remains above Bayes-optimal risk, refining the account of overfitting. It does not directly reproduce the original random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on label-noise profiles, interpolation, and training-time dynamics. It does not test shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs as inputs. Detailed plotted values are not stated in text, so those rows use figure_only.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own neural-network interpolation and label-noise experiments across new datasets and sample sizes, plus signal-versus-noise learning dynamics. Its tempered-overfitting conclusion is compatible with these claim versions; it primarily qualifies benign-overfitting claims outside this list.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The tested interpolating DNNs exhibit tempered overfitting: label noise produces persistent excess test risk, while early stopping can yield approximately benign fitting. These are empirical findings at moderate scale; the authors leave open other regimes for other DNN settings.
record.recipe_differences: Studies label-noise profiles and asymptotic test risk across DNNs and kernel regression, rather than reproducing the original random-label intervention and its full architecture and hyperparameter comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Training stage changes the outcome: early-stopped SVHN ResNets approach benign fitting, while interpolating ResNets show tempered fitting. Dataset, model, sample size, and label-noise level also vary; the paper notes profile differences across settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Early-stopped SVHN ResNets approach low test error despite substantial training-label noise as sample size increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early stopping can reduce the generalization cost of label noise before interpolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Kernel-regression risk depends on the kernel spectrum, ridge parameter, and input dimension.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Kernel methods can exhibit benign, tempered, or catastrophic overfitting under different spectral and regularization conditions.

record.problems: DNN findings are entirely empirical. The paper says its real and synthetic datasets are at most moderate size; it leaves open whether other settings yield benign or catastrophic interpolation. CINIC-10 VGG results use one experiment. Most DNN noise-profile values are plotted rather than stated numerically. The study does not report a direct test-error-at-chance statement for fully random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. Figure-only numerical values were not reconstructed from plots.

untested.parts: Exact chance-level test errors at the maximally randomized endpoints are not readable from the supplied figure text. Fixed-proportion corruption is not an exact replication of independently sampled random labels.
No comparison of convergence time or training cost across true-label and random-label conditions is reported.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment is reported.
Exact pointwise monotonicity and numerical chance endpoints cannot be independently checked from the supplied figure text.

Weight decay and dropout preventing memorization are not tested. Generalization with versus without explicit regularization is not compared. The augmentation evidence concerns random horizontal flips only.
No direct temporal comparison of real-image labels against fully random labels, or example-level tracking of clean versus corrupted classification labels, is reported.

missing.what: The interpolating 3 × 1024 MLP on binary MNIST: Figure 3 reports noise profiles across n = 1,000, 10,000, and 60,000, and Appendix C.3 reports 100% training accuracy and train loss ≤ 1e−4. Add its own row, distinct from nearest-neighbor methods and the one-epoch MLP.

record.verdict_notes: Early stopping does not challenge a claim conditioned on fitting the training set perfectly. Likewise, persistent excess risk at fixed nonzero label noise does not challenge V4. Missing numerical plot values and a single experimental run warrant uncertainty, not limits_scope verdicts by themselves.

versions.untested_parts: Tests interpolation with varying label noise, including fully corrupted binary labels; does not report test error at chance in words or test the original paper's complete settings and hyperparameter comparison.
Does not establish an exact smooth or steadily rising relationship across every noise level in text; most curves are figures. Does not test all networks or datasets.

Tests signal-versus-noise learning over time on a synthetic constant-function regression task with Gaussian observation noise, not real images with random labels or a direct comparison of real-label and random-label learning.

rows.subject: Wide ResNet 28×10
rows.operation_detail: Trained to interpolation on binary CIFAR-10 with varying fractions of labels resampled to the alternative class; clean test classification error measured.

conditions.value: SGD; batch size 128; initial learning rate 0.1; momentum 0.9
no weight decay, dropout, or other regularization; random horizontal flips

rows.measure: Clean test classification error across training label-flip probabilities; training interpolation.
rows.value: Figure 2 shows test error rising with train noise and persisting as n grows; the paper describes the network as trained to interpolation. Numeric values not stated.
rows.note: The paper explicitly says greater train noise results in greater test error and this error persists as n grows. Exact curve values are figure-only.
rows.check: The interpolation and increasing test-error findings are stated in text, not solely figure-only. Random horizontal flips remain enabled, providing evidence for the augmentation component of V5. At p = 0.5 the binary labels have no predictive signal; this is not a setting where every label is flipped. Record the fixed 60-epoch schedule.

rows.measure: Clean test classification error across training label-noise levels; training interpolation.
rows.value: Figure 6a presents a tempered noise profile; numeric values not stated.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over three independent runs; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The text says the interpolating DNN does not approach Bayes optimality and exhibits tempered overfitting in both CIFAR-10 settings.
rows.check: Section 4.2 explicitly describes interpolation and tempered overfitting, although exact test-error values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. rows.subject: 3 × 1024 MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained to interpolation on a synthetic constant-function binary classification task with a fixed proportion of labels flipped; clean test classification error measured.

conditions.value: synthetic inputs sampled from S⁹; ground-truth label is constant 1
SGD; initial learning rate 0.1; momentum 0.9; batch size 128

rows.measure: Clean test classification error across training label-flip probabilities; training interpolation.
rows.value: Figure 6b shows a tempered noise profile; the text says the network does not successfully learn the constant function in the presence of even slight label noise. Numeric values not stated.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over five independent runs; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: Binary task with labels flipped to −1. Training was stopped at the stated MSE threshold.
rows.check: The stopping threshold of train MSE ≤ 1e−4 directly documents near-interpolation. Noise is imposed by flipping a fixed proportion of labels. Learning-rate schedules differ across sample-size groups, although no noise-dependent schedule changes are stated.

conditions.value: two-fold cross-validation selects epoch maximizing validation classification error averaged over folds; first ten epochs excluded

rows.measure: Clean test classification error across training label-noise levels.
rows.value: Figure 7a shows test error approaching zero as n increases, even with finite label noise; described as fairly benign fitting. Numeric values not stated.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard error over three independent runs; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: This is an early-stopped condition, not the interpolating condition named by V4; included as a within-study comparison showing the training-stage dependence.
rows.check: Early-stopped test error does not test V4's conjunction of perfect training fit and rising test error. Remove the reversed state and the V1/V4 scope verdicts based on this row. Appendix C.3 literally says validation error is maximized; this conflicts with the description of optimal early stopping and may be a source typo. Do not silently replace it with minimization.

rows.subject: standard VGG-19 with batch norm
rows.operation_detail: Overfit to CINIC-10 with varying fractions of labels flipped; clean test classification error measured.
rows.measure: Clean test classification error across training label-flip probabilities.
rows.value: Figure 11 shows the overfit VGG-19 noise profile; numeric values not stated.
rows.note: The text characterizes the profile as tempered in Appendix D.2, but reports only one experiment due to computational limitations.
rows.check: Appendix D.2 explicitly characterizes the VGG noise profile as tempered, so cannot_determine is too strong for the qualitative finding. Exact values and an explicit training-error threshold are unavailable. One run limits precision; it does not itself establish a scope failure.

rows.subject: 4 × 512 ReLU MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a synthetic constant-function regression task with Gaussian observation noise; train and test MSE tracked over optimization time.

conditions.value: inputs uniform on S⁴; targets yi = 1 + N(0, 1); clean test labels yi = 1

rows.measure: Train and test MSE over training time.
rows.value: Text says test performance is nearly Bayes-optimal early; after train MSE falls below Bayes risk, train loss continues down while test loss increases, then approaches a finite suboptimal asymptote.
rows.uncertainty: Averaged over five trials; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The text interprets the post-Bayes-risk phase as fitting training noise; this is a synthetic regression task, not real images or fully random labels.
rows.check: The reported test MSE equals clean-target MSE plus 1, making the Bayes baseline 1 correct for the plotted measure. Clarify this construction. Appendix C.3 specifies 4 × 512 units, while Figure 8's caption says 4 × 500; retain that source discrepancy. The experiment tests shared-signal-before-noise dynamics in regression.

relation.reason: Reports original measurements of neural-network interpolation under label corruption, clean test error across noise levels, and signal-versus-noise learning dynamics.

tranche.reason: Own interpolation and noise-profile experiments extend the claim across datasets, sample sizes, and architectures. Persistent excess risk qualifies benign-overfitting claims, without contradicting these random-label claim versions.

source_check.notes: Exact chance-level endpoints are not numerically recoverable; qualitative interpolation and tempered-profile findings are explicitly stated. The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated July 2024, although the record lists the study's 2022 year.
